paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : TriviaQA confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation:
The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" and has a linear scale ranging from 0.71 to 1.00, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. 

The first line, representing "Final Accuracy", is blue with circular markers and a solid line style; it starts at approximately 0.84 at an initial confidence of 0.71, reaches a peak of approximately 0.94 at an initial confidence of 0.82, declines to approximately 0.88 at an initial confidence of 0.96, and finishes at approximately 0.86 at an initial confidence of 1.00. Error bars are present at each data point.

The second line, representing "Δ Accuracy", is orange with diamond markers and a dashed line style; it begins at approximately 0.05 at 0.71 initial confidence, decreases to a minimum of approximately -0.15 at 0.83 initial confidence, rises to approximately 0.09 at 0.95 initial confidence, and ends at approximately 0.03 at 1.00 initial confidence. Error bars are also visible along this line.

The third line, representing "Initial Accuracy", is green with square markers and a dotted line style; it begins at approximately 0.63 at an initial confidence of 0.71, rises to a maximum of approximately 0.89 at an initial confidence of 0.82, declines to approximately 0.75 at an initial confidence of 0.96, and finishes at approximately 0.78 at an initial confidence of 1.00. Error bars are included for this line as well.
